title: ☁️ Host a Website on AWS S3
subtitle: Simple step-by-step guide to hosting your static website on Amazon S3

hero.imageAlt: AWS S3 static site hosting guide

intro.title: Why Host on AWS S3?
paragraphs: Amazon S3 is perfect for hosting static websites - those with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files that don't need server-side processing. It's cost-effective, reliable, and scales automatically with your traffic.
This guide walks you through hosting a single-page site on S3, making it publicly accessible, and optionally adding your own domain name and HTTPS security.
What you'll need: An AWS account and your website files ready to upload.

items.title: Using AWS Console
items.body: Think of an S3 bucket as a folder in the cloud where you'll store your website files. The bucket name must be globally unique.
list: Go to S3 in the AWS Console
Pick a globally unique name, for example mysitename.com

items.title: Upload your site
items.body: Put your index.html and any assets in a local folder on your computer.
list: Drag and drop your files or use Add files

items.title: Turn storage into a website
items.body: This tells S3 to serve your files as a website instead of just storage.

code.content: aws s3 website s3://mysitename.com --index-document index.html --error-document error.html

items.title: Unblock public access
items.body: By default, S3 buckets are private. You need to allow public access so browsers can view your website.

items.title: Add a bucket policy
items.body: Create a policy file and apply it to the bucket.

callout.text: Apply it with: aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket mysitename.com --policy file://policy.json

items.title: Open the endpoint
items.body: Open the S3 website endpoint from Step 3 in your browser. You should see your index.html page.

callout.text: Congratulations! Your website is now live on the internet.

items.title: Custom Domain
items.body: If you own a domain like mysitename.com, you can point it to your S3 website using DNS settings or Route 53.

items.title: HTTPS Security
items.body: S3 websites are HTTP-only. For HTTPS, use CloudFront with an SSL certificate from AWS Certificate Manager.

items.title: Performance
items.body: CloudFront also speeds up your site by caching it at edge locations worldwide.

items.title: Cost
items.body: S3 hosting is very affordable - typically just a few cents per month for small websites.

code.content:
Hello from S3!

This is a single-page site served from S3.

items.title: 403 Forbidden Error
items.body: Check that your bucket policy allows public access and that Block public access is turned off.

items.title: Changes Not Showing
items.body: S3 updates can take a few minutes. Try refreshing your browser or clearing cache.

items.title: Mobile Testing
items.body: Test your site on different devices and browsers to ensure it works well everywhere.

items.title: SEO Friendly
items.body: Include proper meta tags, alt text for images, and descriptive page titles for better search engine visibility.

footer.heading: Thanks for learning AWS S3 hosting with Grandma! ☁️
footer.text: Remember: The cloud is just someone else's computer, but it's a very reliable computer!
